descriptionChirho: To be or become silent, still, or quiet; to refrain from speech or activity. Used of persons keeping silence before God (Ps 37:7 'Be still before the LORD'; Ps 62:5 'For God alone, O my soul, wait in silence'), of silencing opponents (Ps 31:17 'let the wicked be put to silence in Sheol'), and of general stillness or cessation of speech (Lev 10:3 Aaron 'was silent'; Job 29:21; Lam 2:10,18; 3:28). The basic Qal sense covers both voluntary silence and imposed stillness.

To come to a halt, stop moving, or cease activity; physical stillness or cessation of natural motion. Distinguished from simple silence by its spatial/physical reference. Most notably in Joshua's command to the sun at Gibeon (Josh 10:12-13 'Sun, stand still at Gibeon... and the sun stood still'); also of standing still to witness divine action (1 Sam 14:9); and of ceasing from turmoil (Job 30:27; Ps 35:15).

To be forcibly silenced, destroyed, or cut off; passive or resultative cessation implying annihilation or divine judgment. Predominantly Nifal stems conveying involuntary destruction: the wicked silenced in darkness (1 Sam 2:9), nations silenced before God's judgment (Jer 8:14; 25:37; 49:26; 50:30; 51:6). Often paired with perishing, as in Korean/Spanish glosses 'perish, be destroyed,' indicating not mere quietness but total cessation of existence.

To cause to become quiet or calm; intensive-causative silencing directed toward soothing or composing another. Attested in Ps 131:2 where the psalmist says 'I have calmed and quieted my soul,' using the Piel to express deliberate, gentle pacification of one's own inner turmoil. Distinguished from Hifil by the absence of destructive connotation and the focus on nurturing stillness.

To bring to silence by causing destruction or annihilation; causative silencing with a connotation of divine judgment or punitive force. Attested in Jer 8:14 where God 'has silenced us' (הֲדִמָּנוּ), referring to the devastating judgment that reduces a people to silence. The Hifil form marks the external agent who imposes silence through overwhelming, destructive power, distinguishing it from the gentler Piel causative.
